To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nitric oxide and nitrate ions are capable of binding to cytochrome d of Escherichia col i.

the absorbance maximum ( 630 nm) of cytochrome c oxidase in Escherichi a coli is diminished by nitrate or nitrite, but not by silver, ions, and that nitrite or nitrate ions are more potent than silver ions in inhibiting the electron transfer activity of cytochrome oxidase.
nitrate and nitrite ions, but not silver ions, induce spectral changes in cytochrome d.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of silver and nitrate ions, and their derivatives, on cytochrome d and other cytochromes of E. coli.
the effect of nitrite, nitrate and nitric oxides on the spectral characteristics of cytochrome b d 1.
the effects of nitrite, nitrate, nitric oxide and silver ions on the spectral properties of cytochrome cbb3 (d) of Escherichia colt and the possible role of the cytochrome in nitrite reduction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nitrate and silver ions induce spectral changes of cytochrome c in the same manner as NO and that nitrate and NO induce spectral changes of the same nature in cytochromes c and d.
nitrate, nitrite and nitric oxide induce a change in the reduced cytochrome spectrum which is consistent with a nitrosyl‐cytochrome complex, whereas Ag1+ does not induce a similar change.
the nitrosyl‐cytochrome d complex is formed with nitrite, trioxonitrate and nitric oxides, but not nitrate or silver ions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of Ag + and NO 3 − on cytochrome d are qualitatively similar but quantitatively distinct.
the nitrate‐induced changes in cytochrome d are similar, if not identical, to those induced by nitrite or nitric oxide.
silver ions, but not nitrate ions, are able to inhibit the electron transfer from cytochrome c to cytochrome d.
The main takeaway from our work is that

nitrate and nitrite are capable of interacting directly with cytochrome d to produce spectral changes similar to those elicited by nitric oxide, and that silver ions are not effective at inducing spectral changes in the cytochrome d heme.
silver ions do not affect the redox state of cytochrome oxidase in vivo and therefore are not likely to have any direct toxic effects on the respiratory system.
the effects of nitrate on cytochrome d are not mediated by silver ions, but may be related to the formation of a nitroso complex with cytochrome d.
